ranking.title: 211.84 Testing and approval or rejection of components, drug product containers, and closures.

rows.context: 211.194 Laboratory records. > Laboratory records shall include complete data derived from all tests necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, including examinations and assays, as follows:
rows.text: A description of the sample received for testing with identification of source (that is, location from where sample was obtained), quantity, lot number or other distinctive code, date sample was taken, and date sample was received for testing.

passages.text:
1. Purpose

To set out what the record of every laboratory test must hold and how test records are checked, for raw materials, containers, closures, in-process samples and finished products tested in the Chennai QC laboratory.

3. The test record

3.1 Each sample is entered in the sample register when it arrives, with where it was taken from, the quantity, the lot or receipt number, the date it was taken and the date it was received. 3.2 The analyst writes on the worksheet the method used, by number, and the specification tested against. For a pharmacopoeial method the worksheet names the monograph and its edition; for an in-house method it names the validation report that holds the method's accuracy and precision data. 3.3 The weight or volume of sample taken for each test is written on the worksheet. 3.4 Every chro

5. Other laboratory records

5.1 Reference standards, reagents and volumetric solutions are logged when received or prepared, and every standardisation is recorded with its result, the date and the analyst's initials. 5.2 Stability test results are recorded in the stability database under SOP-QC-014.
